items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7317

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general business law, in relation to debt
management services; and to amend the banking law, in relation to the
uniform debt-management services act; and repealing certain provisions
of such laws relating thereto


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to protect consumers from unfair and
deceptive practices in the debt management services industry by
expanding state oversight of the industry and implementing several new
consumer protections.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill would enact the Uniform Debt-Management Services Act. The
Act require entities that offer to serve as an intermediary between an
individual and one or more creditors of the individual for the purpose
of obtaining concessions, often referred to as debt management
services, to register with the Banking Department.  Registration would
require submission of detailed information concerning the service,
including its financial condition, the identity of principals,
locations at which service will be offered, form for agreements with
debtors and operational history in other jurisdictions. To register, a
service must have an effective insurance policy against fraud,
dishonesty, and theft in an amount no less than $250,000. It must also
provide a surety bond of a minimum of $50,000.

The bill would require debt management services to provide debtors
with certain disclosures regarding fees and the services to be
offered, and the risks and benefits of entering into such a contract.
Services would be required to offer counseling services from a
certified counselor or certified debt specialist and a plan must be
created in consultation with the counselor for debt management service
activities to commence.

The bill specifies the contents of the agreements and fees that may be
charged. The bill provides for a penalty-free three-day right of
rescission on the part of the debtor, as well as a restricted 30-day
period cancellation period. Any payments for creditors received from a
debtor would be required to be kept in a trust account that may not be
used to hold any other funds of the service. The bill provides for
strict accounting requirements and periodic reporting requirements
respecting funds held.

The bill prohibits specific acts on the part of a service including:
misappropriation of funds in trust; settlement for more than fifty
percent of a debt with a creditor without a debtor's consent; gifts or
premiums to enter into an agreement; and representation that
settlement has occurred without certification from a creditor. The
bill provides for enforcement by the Banking Department and private
individuals. The Department would have investigative powers, power to
order an individual to cease and desist; power to assess a civil
penalty up to $10,000, and the power to bring a civil action. An
individual would be authorized to bring a civil action for
compensatory damages, including triple damages if a service obtains
payments not authorized in the Article, and may seek punitive damages
and attorney's fees.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Advertisements for entities offering debt management services, which
include credit counseling, debt consolidation, debt management, and
debt settlement, have become ubiquitous. Many debt-laden consumers are
confused as to which entities offering help are legitimate.  Calls for
stronger oversight of debt management services have increased in
recent years. Several witnesses at the December 1, 2008, Assembly
hearing on Senior Scams recommended that the State increase its
regulation of the debt management services industry. The U.S.  Senate
Homeland Security and Governmental Affair's Investigative
Subcommittee, the Consumer Federation of America, and the National
Consumer Law Center have all issued reports in the past five years
documenting abuses in the industry.

This comprehensive uniform act drafted by the National Conference of
Commissioners on Uniform State Laws is aimed at reining in the
excesses of the debt management services industry while allowing such
services to continue to provide services that benefit consumers. The
Act provides guidance and regulation to the consumer credit counseling
and debt settlement industries. The Act is a comprehensive statute
that provides rules for, among other things, registration
requirements, bond requirements, certification requirements,
disclosure requirements, and penalties for non-compliance.

The need for uniform state laws in this area increased significantly
following the enactment of the Bankruptcy Abuse Prevention and
Consumer Protection Act (BAPCPA) of 2005. Pursuant to the BAPCPA, most
individuals filing for Chapter 7 bankruptcy are required to show that
credit counseling and debt education/management has been sought and
attempted. This shifts a highly significant burden upon private
services to perform honestly and effectively. Because the new
bankruptcy rules are federal and apply in every state, regulating the
debt management services industry in every state must be uniform in
character for the new bankruptcy rules to be effective and for
consumers to be protected. At least four other states have adopted the
Act or a modified version of the Act since it was finalized in 2005.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
One year after enactment.

summary: Establishes the uniform debt-management services act.
